title: Product: vision, strategy, specification, roadmap and backlog
vision: Every young person in the UK knows how to make their voice heard, and is heard, safely.
mission: Carry youth voice further: bring together trusted sources, safe routes into participation and campaign tools for young people, and for the adults who support them, across all four nations.

strategy.what: Every fact sourced and dated; models, samples and generated text labelled; checks that prove it on every change.
Safeguarding first, no personal data, age-appropriate routes, adults acting on a young person's behalf where needed.
Accessible to WCAG 2.2 AA, pan-UK, every voice and language, including sign languages.
User-centred design, open research, contributions and ambassadors, all in the open.
Self-checking, self-reporting and updated every week, with people deciding anything irreversible.

spec.what: An independent, unofficial, open-source web portal about youth voice and participation in the UK.
spec.who: Young people aged 11 to 25, parents and carers, youth workers, teachers, club leaders, and adult allies such as councillors, researchers and journalists.
in: Routes into youth voice by age and nation
Get involved: contribute, research, ambassadors, campaign kit, training, STEM and tech
out: Acting for, or speaking as, the UK Youth Parliament, NYA or UK Parliament
constraints: No request to another host when a page loads
Contact by form only, never an email address
Everything generated from data; nothing hand-edited in the built site

schedule.what: What's new and the news ticker
schedule.when: Weekly, and straight away for anything safety-critical
With every release that adds a term
When the owner merges a reviewed pull request

github.what: Ideas, bugs, contact, research interest and ambassador interest arrive through public issue forms that ask for no personal details.
A workflow thanks the person, labels the issue for triage, and flags anything that looks like personal data so it can be removed.
Each week the upkeep run decides: accept, adapt, defer or decline, with a reason. Accepted items become requirements here (REQ ids).
Changes are made in data/ or tools/ on a branch; a pull request links the requirement and issue it serves.
Every check runs on every pull request, in a real browser too; each requirement names the checks that prove it.
The owner merges and republishes; the release log and drawer flags update from data/changelog.json.
Every Monday a workflow gathers what is due: open items, gates not passed, overdue sources and coming dates, into one Follow-ups issue.
